newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-FOCUS - Woolworths tips steady gains.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-FOCUS - Woolworths tips steady gains.

text.p: Australia's largest grocery retailer, Woolworths Ltd, tipped steady sales and profit growth for the rest of the 1996/97 financial year on Monday, based on signs of improved consumer confidence in Australia.
"We are confident we can maintain current sales predictions and profit growth for the remainder of this financial year," managing director Reg Clairs told a news conference.
Woolworths earlier reported an 8.62 percent rise in net profit to A$147.5 million for the 28 weeks ended January 5 on sales of A$8.22 billion, which were up 8.61 percent.
The result was slightly above analysts' forecast range of between A$143 million to A$147 million.
"The (sales) trend generally immediately following Christmas was quite good - overall January was quite strong and February a little softer in relative terms but still quite strong," Clairs said.

Clairs said he saw no return to double digit sales growth in the current low inflation environment and said he would be happy if Woolworths achieved sales growth of 8.5 percent over the next 12 months.
"Our biggest challenge is containing our costs of running the business."
Woolworths was keeping an eye on its rent costs after recent rate increases in some major shopping centres, Clairs said.
"We've seen rent escalations in there that probably are in excess of what we would determine are correct," he said.
However, in general Woolworths had long term leases and the company was managing its leasehold and rent costs appropriately, he said.

"In many of the large shopping centres the small tenants are paying a mandatory increase per annum of five or six percent irrespective of whatever their sales are and that is an issue for the community at large," said the head of Woolworths general merchandise division, Roger Corbett.
Woolworths was pleased with the progress of the petrol outlets it was trialling at six of its supermarkets, John Brunton, the head of Woolworths supermarket division, said.
"Certainly the performance in all those six has been beyond our original projections so we are very happy with it and will continue to roll them out as quickly as possible," he said.
Brunton said Woolworths had another 40 sites that had been approved or were in the process or being approved and an additional 100 sites were on the drawing board.

In a separate announcement, Woolworths said it planned to expand its wholesaling operations through Australian Independent Wholesalers Pty Ltd (AIW), which acquired in July last year as part of its purchase of the Cannons group of stores.
Clairs said the company's decision to expand AIW followed approaches to the company by independent supermarkets and after researching the market.
"We would argue that we're not simply a food retailer, we're in the business of food distribution. That's been evidence by our move into food export and a number of other initiatives," Clairs said.
He said at this stage Woolworths had not signed up any new independent supermarkets and as yet it had not made a significant investment in the expansion.
Later on Monday, Quensland-based buying agent Retail Services Ltd (RSL) said it would not change its current wholesaling arrangements with wholesaler Davids Ltd.

RSL, which buys groceries for about 450 independent supermarkets, said the Woolworths plan to supply Queensland independent supermarkets would further divide the independent market and could lead to more family-owned stores closing.
